notes: CANDIDATE ENTRY -- access terms only partly verified. Corrects a wrong assumption in the task brief: github.com/facebookresearch/Embody3D (as originally guessed) 404s because the real repo is hyphenated and lower-case, github.com/facebookresearch/embody-3d (confirmed reachable, has a README and download.py). Paper (arXiv:2510.16258, submitted 17 Oct 2025, 8 pages per local PDF extraction -- NOT 4 pages as an earlier automated page-count estimate suggested) verified directly from the fetched PDF text: 'The Codec Avatars Lab at Meta introduces Embody 3D, a multimodal dataset of 500 individual hours of 3D motion data from 439 participants collected in a multi-camera collection stage, amounting to over 54 million frames of tracked 3D motion.' Seven categories: Charades, Hand Interactions, Locomotion, Dyadic Conversations, Multi-Person Conversations, Scenarios, Day in the Life. Includes hand tracking, body shape/SMPL-X-style tracked motion, text annotations, and per-participant separated audio. IMPORTANT: the arXiv paper text contains NO occurrence of 'IMU', 'inertial', or 'license' anywhere in its body (checked by full-text search of the extracted PDF) -- this is multi-camera markerless motion capture, not inertial sensor data, consistent with AMASS/Motion-X's role here as a synthetic-IMU source rather than real wearable-sensor data. Access mechanics (from the repo README, not the paper): fill out a release form at the meta.com project page; approval yields 21 per-category/per-modality download links compiled into a text file and fetched with `python src/download.py --src download.txt` (filterable by --feat / --category). The repo explicitly warns downloads are blocked without the signed release form. Could NOT independently confirm the exact legal text of the Meta XRCIA licence from this machine -- flagging this as the honest state rather than asserting terms. Verified 2026-09-09.
